recommendation: Do not publish 09-talents-abilities as it stands. Reject the chapter pending (1) the eight chapter-local mechanical fixes, (2) the book-wide band and crossref reconciliations that cannot be done in this file alone, and (3) one principal ruling on whether a higher-band weapon maneuver keeps the outcome block it prints or comes down to the Novice row. The chapter is a complete 72-card library and its hierarchy, pagination and basic-attack numbers are sound; what fails is its damage rows, its tier legibility, and its restatements of rules owned by other chapters.
rationale:
SCOPE AND OUTCOME
This run tested 09-talents-abilities against three topics: t-01 conformance to the locked conventions, t-02 internal consistency, and t-03 cross-chapter canon. The engine closed all three rejected: t-01 conformance, 5 refutes / 0 support; t-02 internal consistency, 7 refutes / 0 support; t-03 cross-chapter canon, 5 refutes / 0 support. No sealed rulings were issued, so rulings_applied is empty and nothing in this plan is court-ordered. Twenty-eight findings were filed (f-001..f-028, one round, real paths unmodified). Two member findings still carry support stances -- librarian f-019 on t-01 and layout-expert f-015 on t-02 -- and both are preserved verbatim under dissent as minority positions; neither contradicts the engine's recorded tallies. Facts marked ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED were reproduced by the orchestrator against the registered source, the book and the built PDF (386 pages, built 2026-09-15 14:49) rather than taken from a lens filing; they were not filed by any member.

WHY THE CHAPTER FAILS
t-01: six weapon maneuvers print the retired Novice band as one figure per outcome line (invisible to a grep for the closed triplet), six more print the Adept or Master row as an outcome block, Death Blow carries the book's only 'maximum 21' against a core-chapter cap of 14, Parry pays a 2 that sits on no live row, and nine maneuver headers drop 13 rank numerals. t-02: the maneuver introduction states one damage row while its own cards implement three, the Basic Attacks introduction promises four universal cards that each carry a Kit gate, seven talents print no tier so neither price nor level gate is readable from the card, and three openers describe card classes the file does not contain. t-03: Death Blow's ceiling, Parry's counterattack figure, Miracle Worker's proportional healing, the two spell-recast talents against the magic chapter's casting brake, and four effects duplicated from the classes chapter.

PLAN
The tier labels are the problem statement's; each item gives the site, the exact change, and the finding id(s) or the ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED tag.

TIER 1 -- MECHANICAL (chapter-local, no mechanics change: wording, stale figures, crossrefs, typography)
M-1. [09-talents-abilities:220-224, :238-242, :265-269, :310-314, :319-323, :364-368] Bring the six cards that spell the retired Novice band one figure per line onto the live Novice row 4/6/8: Riposte's counterattack 2/4/6 -> 4/6/8; Cyclone 2/4/6 -> 4/6/8; Shield Slam 2/4/6 -> 4/6/8; Brace's retaliation 2/4/6 -> 4/6/8; Renewal's healing 2/4/6 -> 4/6/8; Dual Strike's two attacks each dealing 1/2/3 with totals 2/4/6 -> each dealing 2/3/4 with totals 4/6/8. Nothing else on these cards moves. Findings f-009, f-025, f-028, f-001; f-019 reads the same class but counts five of the six (it takes Riposte's counterattack as a payout rather than a damage line). Band, site list, totals and the per-line form are ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED.
M-2. [09-talents-abilities:78] Death Blow: change the cap on its one-row Critical bump from 21 to 14, matching 06-core-resolution.qmd:168 where the identical raise is capped, or strike the parenthetical as inert. 21 is the book's only occurrence of that figure as damage and the live Master row stops at 14. Findings f-012, f-008, f-004, f-027; single occurrence and the 06 cap are ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED.
M-3. [09-talents-abilities:278] Parry: change the Strong-rung counterattack from 2 to 4 so the payout sits on the Novice row the introduction at :215 assigns to a maneuver's figures; if a floor-grade jab is intended instead, the card must state the basis it pays from (basic attacks are 1/2/3 plus Brawn). The DR ladder itself (:274-276) is legal under convention 6 and stays; only the damage figure is off any live row. Findings f-011, f-027.
M-4. [09-talents-abilities:461, :470, :479, :488, :497, :533, :542, :551, :560] Type the 13 missing rank numerals on these nine maneuver headers in the chapter's own explicit form (:156, :515, :569, e.g. 3 Archery - 1 Tactics - 1 Stealth). Reflow nothing; no prose change. Findings f-013; the 13 bare tokens, the nine headers, and the ch11/ch12 comparison (50 and 34 numbered tokens) are ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED.
M-5. [09-talents-abilities:33, :98, :143, :148, :153, :158, :163] Seven talents open their effect line with the tier-neutral Effect label and no card in the file prints a tier, so the tier-derived price (2/4/8 DP) and level gate (1/3/7) cannot be read off a card. Fix either at :15 (add the tier to the header lesson, one edit covering all 72 cards) or on the seven labels (print the tier word, as the other 21 talents do). Findings f-005, f-028.
M-6. [09-talents-abilities:15] Name the Kit field in the header lesson (twelve cards carry it, none of its six tags defined in-file) and route its vocabulary to 15-equipment.qmd; route the Keywords field's 35 distinct tags to the template section of 19-gm-guidance.qmd or to 21-glossary.qmd. Findings f-006.
M-7. [09-talents-abilities:13, :213] Trim two openers to what the cards demonstrate: the Action field does not separate a standing benefit from a limited one (15 Passive talents, four of them carrying a use ceiling), and the maneuver opener names two non-weapon gates while at least nine maneuvers are gated on armour, protection or tactics. Findings f-021, f-024.
M-8. Correct the run record, not the chapter: the census is 28 Talents / 4 Basic Attacks / 40 Weapon Maneuvers / 72 cards in 577 lines, not the brief's 29/4/39, and the verification string the brief attributes to the 11 September run is a Wave-1 row dated 23-24 August. No chapter edit follows. Findings f-019, f-020, f-015; census and line count are ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED.

TIER 2 -- SUBSTANTIVE (new content, multi-file, or a reconciliation touching more than one card)
S-1. [09-talents-abilities:83, :98] Arcane Reservoir and The Full Ledger recharge spells past the brake the magic chapter owns (an Adept or Master spell once a combat, a Master spell once a session), and :17 lets separate talents stack, so one Master spell can land five times in a three-scene session. Re-scope or re-cost both against 10-magic-system.qmd, and give both a legible frequency and a tier marker. Finding f-003.
S-2. [09-talents-abilities:247-251] Cleave prints the same line on all three rungs and states its damage only by reference to the first hit's, so the card carries no figure. Print the band each rung deals, or an explicit exemption. Finding f-028.
S-3. [09-talents-abilities:88] Miracle Worker heals a share of the ally's maximum HP; the reference sheet requires flat values for abilities and the book's only proportional recovery is a combat action, not a card. Rewrite to a flat figure. Finding f-027.
S-4. [09-talents-abilities:28, :33, :68, :98, :123, :265-269] Fold or cut the in-file duplicates and reconcile the four pairs shadowing class and ancestry effects: Turn the Bones folds into The Full Ledger; keep one of Fortune's Favor / Chaotic Insight; Guarding Stance, Riposte, Shield Slam and Miracle Worker each need a cross-reference or a cut against their 05-classes.qmd twins (the riposte twin still prints a stale flat 2 at 05:684 and the Miracle Worker twin restores 1 HP at Master, so the higher tier is the weaker card). Findings f-023, f-024.
S-5. [09-talents-abilities:289, :298, :343] Rename or cross-reference the three cards whose names double as rule terms owned elsewhere: Trip (13-combat.qmd shared-effects table, 21-glossary.qmd, 22-reference-sheets.qmd), Charge (the mounted rule in 15-equipment.qmd, plus 20-bestiary.qmd traits), Throw (the grapple option in 13-combat.qmd). 07-skills.qmd's open disclosure for Parry is the handling to copy. Finding f-022.
S-6. Book-wide retired-band residue, routed to open issue #546 and not fixable chapter-locally: 11-arcane-spells.qmd:171-175, 08-disciplines.qmd:226, 20-bestiary.qmd:142, plus 05-classes.qmd:656 and :684. The 08 and 20 lines are conforming restatements of ch11's still-stale card and must move with it, not in isolation. Findings f-025, f-009, f-017; all five sites ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED. f-017 additionally corrects the run's own conventions: the no-weapon-damage rule lives in 15-equipment.qmd rather than 16-armor-shields.qmd, and the retired band is not confined to ch11/ch12.
S-7. [09-talents-abilities:15 twice, :169, :213] Recast this chapter's four mid-sentence crossrefs so the reference ends its sentence -- but as part of a book-wide sweep: the construction occurs 103 times book-wide, 49 of them rendering with a stranded period in the built PDF, so a chapter-local fix would leave the convention broken. Finding f-014; book-wide count ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED.
S-8. [09-talents-abilities:217-575] Give the 40-card maneuver run a finding aid: reorder the cards so they share a gating Discipline contiguously, or add a grouped name list to the section introduction. 22-reference-sheets.qmd carries no card index and the chapter's own Contents stops at the three section openers. Finding f-016.
S-9. [21-glossary.qmd] The glossary defines a weapon maneuver as a spend of the Maneuver resource and cites a Reaction card and an Action card from this chapter as its examples; the cards own the usage, so the definition is what moves. Finding f-027.
S-10. [09-talents-abilities:23; 15-equipment.qmd:29, :121, :123] The kit-grant sentence promises a card class no card anywhere inhabits; trim the sentence and its equipment-chapter mirror together, or give the category a member in a later content pass. Findings f-024, f-028, f-006.
S-11. [21-glossary.qmd] The 'most talents are passive' description this file prints at :13 is carried in the glossary too, so the M-7 wording fix must reach both files together. Findings f-021, f-028.

TIER 3 -- DESIGN (a fork with two defensible readings that this council cannot settle by reading the file)
D-1. [09-talents-abilities:460, :469, :487, :514, :532, :568; values at :463-467, :472-476, :490-494, :517-521, :535-539, :571-575] Fork: does a higher-band maneuver keep the outcome block it prints, or come down to the Novice row? Reading (a): the maneuver introduction's first clause binds a maneuver's three-line block to the Novice row, and convention 3 restates that as the ruled law -- decision #103 (Option A, ruled by the principal 2026-09-12, shipped in PR #488 / commit 115f18d, which also corrected Shield Slam) makes the maneuver base the Novice row; the live Novice row is 4/6/8, so all six come down. Reading (b): the same sentence's second clause gives the higher-tier family members their own rows and names, 21-glossary.qmd:43 describes the same table as what a damaging maneuver keys to, and the six cards' figures track their implied tier exactly (four at 5/8/11, two at 7/10/14), so the six are Adept and Master cards priced 4 and 8 DP and gated at levels 3 and 7. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: (a), anchored on the ruled law (decision #103) and locked convention 3; it is also the reading that lets M-1 fix all twelve off-row maneuver cards in one pass. Note that #103's vocabulary predates the one-card refactor (#537/#538, landed the day after), so it does not by itself settle the current card shape; the card-shape question -- whether an Adept or Master card prints a single Effect line instead of an outcome block -- remains open as decisions-pending #124, which is STILL OPEN on 2026-09-15. IF THE PRINCIPAL REVERSES TO (b): rewrite :215's first clause to scope the Novice-row claim, add a tier field (price and gate) to the header lesson at :15, re-author the six in the single-Effect-line shape #124 defines, and re-open the cost-to-row binding in 10-magic-system.qmd for maneuvers. Findings f-010, f-018, f-026, f-007, f-001.
D-2. [09-talents-abilities:169, :174, :183, :192, :201] Fork: are the four Basic Attacks gated by their Kit tags, or open to every character? Reading (a): 15-equipment.qmd owns kit law and makes a kit the permission settling which cards a character may use, re-fittable only in town, and all four cards carry a tag, so the intro's blanket promise is what must be rescoped. Reading (b): the section presents the four as a universal floor, so the kit law needs a carve-out -- but then the unarmed tag becomes decorative, colliding with the equipment rule that a Kit field appears only where the work needs the tool. Neither chapter states the priority. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: (a), anchored on the owning chapter's kit law and on this chapter's own restatements yielding to the chapter that owns the rule; the visible cost is that a two-handed or ranged class hero may own none of the four, which also makes Follow My Lead :436-440 and Eyes On Me :445-449 hand an ally an attack that ally may not own. IF THE PRINCIPAL REVERSES TO (b): 15-equipment.qmd's kit law and its 'only where the work needs the tool' clause must be rewritten to exempt the four, and the two support maneuvers re-scoped with it. Finding f-002.

SEQUENCING AND WHAT MUST NOT GO CHAPTER-LOCAL
Land M-1..M-8 and D-1's recommended default in one pass over the Weapon Maneuvers section, so the twelve off-row cards move together. Land S-6 with issue #546 and S-7 as the book-wide sweep; a fix confined to this file would leave 08-disciplines teaching the retired row, 20-bestiary printing it as a stat line and 103 crossrefs still rendering with a stranded period. Hold D-2 for the principal; keep #124 as the tracked prerequisite for D-1's reversal path. Every item above is traceable to a ledger finding id or is marked ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED; no number in this plan was invented.

dissent.position: Measured from the file: 72 cards, of which 28 are Talents, 4 are Basic Attacks and 40 are Weapon Maneuvers; the brief states 29 and 39 for the last two families and 72 overall, so the total holds and the split does not. Thirteen of the forty-four cards that print an outcome block sit on a live band: three basic attacks and the unarmed one on the basic floor, three Novice maneuvers on 4/6/8, four Adept maneuvers on 5/8/11 and two Master maneuvers on 7/10/14. Four cards print the retired Novice band with each value written out separately, and a fifth prints it inside its parenthetical running totals, so five cards carry the stale band and eleven sit on a live one. The remaining cards in the block-printing population carry movement, DR or rider figures rather than a damage band, and the 28 Talents carry no band at all because a passive card prints a single effect. No card restates a general rule belonging to another chapter. This file's restatement surface is its prose: the card-format paragraph repeats the price and gate law of the disciplines chapter and the card-shape law of the magic chapter, and the maneuver introduction repeats the equipment chapter's weapon law, while the two-number range note is the one piece the reference sheets delegate here, which makes this file the owner of it. Every card carries its full header and no outcome block is truncated or missing, so the chapter is a complete library in the standalone form.

The chapter's hierarchy and card grammar survive both the source and the print. Level 2 appears exactly three times - the section openers at L21, L167 and L211 - and level 3 only for cards: 72 of them, nothing at level 4, and every card's family suffix matches the section it sits in (28 Talent, 4 Basic Attack, 40 Weapon Maneuver, zero strays), so no section mixes families. The split the brief circulates (29/4/39) is one card off; counted two independent ways - level-3 headings per section, and body shape - the live file reads 28 talents and 40 maneuvers for the same 72 total. Card bodies take exactly two shapes: 44 print a header line plus the three outcome lines, 28 print a header plus a single line (21 of those named for the tier, 7 as an effect). The print agrees with the source: the Contents carries section 11.1 at 147, 11.2 at 152 and 11.3 at 154 and nothing else for this chapter, so no card heading leaks upward into the Contents - the property that keeps a 72-card reference usable - and all 72 cards render one caret heading and one header paragraph, five of those headers wrapping to a second line with no field lost. Pagination is sound as well: four #pagebreak() calls exist (L11, L19, L165, L209), not the three the brief assumes, and each lands on an opener or a section seam, so each family begins at the top of a fresh page; across pages 146-165 no card is split over a page boundary. The price of those breaks is visible and acceptable: three part-filled pages (146 carrying the opener prose, 151 two cards, 153 one card) and a one-card final page 165.
